body:
Review fixes for the review of 06:46 UTC (head `edb566d33`). The maintainer ordered the takeover (issue #2561, comment 7003005333).

New head: `57756c69a65af25691c2094b61ed6d58a6c528b0`.

Finding 1 (`departed` drops a return cut):
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/tab_clear.rs`, `departed` (lines 164-207): the function drops only the monotonic exit. This is the part of the keep where the distance from the tab line keeps growing. A piece that comes nearer to the line than the farthest point before it starts the counted part. This applies also inside `reach` and before the keep is `W + D` away.
- `nearest_other` (lines 115-162, the one-keep leads at lines 153-159): with one keep (`m == 1`), the lead-in and the lead-out join the tab at both ends. They are now read through `departed` too.
- New test: `a_tab_that_a_u_turn_in_a_shallow_notch_cuts_into_holds_the_loop` in `crates/motion/tests/contour_tab_necks.rs`. It uses your 18 mm notch (floor at `y = 22.0`, `D = 6`, `W = 4`, two tabs, start `(22.0, 30.0)`). The loop is held with "passes 4.000 mm from the tab". It failed on `edb566d33` (0 holds).

Finding 2 (`fit_loops` ignores `lad`):
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour.rs` lines 121-124: the tabbed levels of each loop come from `lad.ring(li)` and go to `fit_loops`.
- `tab_clear.rs` `fit_loops` (lines 20-46): no fit when no loop walks a tabbed level.
- `tab_clear.rs` `fit_band` (lines 48-75): a ring with no tabbed level is not checked. Ring `ri` is read against the tabs of ring `i` only when the two rings share a tabbed level.
- New test: `a_ring_that_stops_above_the_tabs_does_not_hold_another_loop` in `contour_tab_necks.rs`. It uses `contour_on_part` on two islands 10 mm apart, `stepdown = 1.0`. The second island stands on a shelf at Z = -1. The test asserts no hold, a cut of the deep island at Z = -4, and no cut of the shelf ring below Z = -1. It failed on `edb566d33` (the deep island was held).

Gate on the new head:
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 160 steps, 0 failed, 41.3 min. `contour_tab_necks` has 7 tests now.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- The PR merged cleanly with `origin/main`, so no merge of main was made.

Not exercised:
- A pinning test for the one-keep leads. I did not find a cheap fixture where a lead turns back toward its tab.
- Inside contours with tabs in a small bore. By the new rule, the far side of a ring nearer than `D` holds the loop, because it cuts into the tab.
- The full batch gate, the release gate and the ignored heavy tests.

Follow-up: #2734 (`lead_held` reads the moved first cut as the picked start point). It is not changed here.

The decision file `docs/decisions/2561-tab-bridge-all-cuts.md` has a new section for these fixes. Your entry did not change.

The push of the takeover is done.

Review by SlaveSession. Built locally in a reviewer worktree. The trial merge with main (21c31e35b) is clean.

**P1 floor: second review needed.** This PR fixes P1 #2561 (a bridge narrower than the tab width). Per AGENTS.md the merge takes a read-only Opus review in addition to this one. Do not merge on this marker alone.

Gate result: contour_tab_necks 7 passed. contour_tab_bridge 9 passed. motion lib tab filter 3 passed. Clippy is clean with -D warnings.

What I verified:
- The gouge law: a cut nearer than D to the tab line holds the loop (it cuts into the tab). A dip to under D is never read as a clear. `departed` counts a piece whose nearest approach is under peak - SLACK from the turn, so a U-turn in a shallow notch holds. NaN reads as a touch. The box test cannot miss a hit: it rejects only pieces wholly outside the need-expanded box.
- The two review findings from head edb566d33 are fixed as the body says, each with its pin: the turn-back read (`a_tab_that_a_u_turn_in_a_shallow_notch_cuts_into_holds_the_loop`) and the level scope (`fit_loops` takes the tabbed levels from the depth ladder; `a_ring_that_stops_above_the_tabs_does_not_hold_another_loop` pins both directions - a false hold on a clear path is also a defect).
- `ring_cuts` sorts keeps by arc position; the tab j is read between cuts j and j+1 with the wrap. One-keep rings take the third of the walk as the reach bound.
- The bridge test reads the posted arcs in chords of 1e-5 mm and pins 1e-4 mm; the decision file gives the bound argument for SLACK 1e-6 without a margin, and names the dropped margin choice.
- Notes: TabFit note becomes notes; `cached` de-dupes. contour.rs fits all rings before the level loop - one fit per ring, as before.

Not exercised (body says so): inside contours with leads at a tab. The rule argument (two runs less than D apart hold) is stated but not run in a test.

Verdict: merge-ready, with the P1 second review as the gate to merge.

Second review (read-only, Opus, P1 floor) of head `57756c69a65af25691c2094b61ed6d58a6c528b0`. Result: one blocker. The merge is held. The reviewer read the code and did not run it.

**Blocker: `departed` drops a return run that goes along the tab and does not come nearer to it.**
`crates/motion/src/machining2d/tab_clear.rs`, lines 171-205, called at lines 137-152.

`departed` counts a later piece only when the piece comes nearer to the tab line than the walk was before (`low < peak - SLACK`). When the walk goes round the bottom of a notch, the far leg stays at a constant distance from the tab. Then no piece is nearer than the peak, and the check drops the full leg as a departure.

Scenario to confirm with a shape-mask probe:

- Geometry of the test in this PR: `notched_to(10.0, 15.0)`, D = 6, W = 4, outside contour, `Lead::None`.
- One change: `start_point = (32, 20)`. This point is on the return leg, 2 mm above the notch bottom.
- The tab ends at the pick and grows backward only. The tab line covers leg 2 from y = 20 to 18, the bottom from x = 32 to 28, and leg 1 from y = 18 upward.
- The cut after the tab goes up leg 2 at x = 32, 4 mm from the tab line on leg 1, for about 20 mm.
- The distance from the tab line goes from 0 to 4 and stays at 4. The "turns back" branch does not operate. There is no hold and no note.
- Expected result: the kerf of leg 2 (x 29..35) overlaps the tab on leg 1 (x 25..31). With `tab_count = 1` the part is cut free at the last tabbed level without a message.

The rule: the check misses each tab whose end is at or after the near bottom corner of a notch, when the notch is less than 2 D wide. A tab end exactly at the corner (a = 0) is missed too. A picked start point lets a user get this case directly.

A possible correction: decide the departure by arc length along the tab line, or by the angle of the walk, not by "the distance does not decrease".

**Should fix: the tests do not pin this scenario.** `crates/motion/tests/contour_tab_necks.rs`: the two U-turn tests pick at (28, 30) on leg 1, thus the tab ends before the corner. These cases have no test:

- a tab end on the notch bottom or on the return leg
- a tab end exactly at the corner
- a V-notch
- an inside contour (the 60 x 7 slot that the PR body names as not run)
- leads together with the neck check
- one keep (`tab_count = 1`) together with a U-turn

**Notes (no blockers):**

- `tab_clear.rs:66`: the shared-level filter compares exact `f64` Z values. Rings with off-grid floors are not compared. The reviewer judged this safe, because a ring that stops above the bottom leaves material below it.
- `tab_clear.rs:59`: a ring that is held can still hold its neighbour. This gives more material and a note, thus it is safe.
- The PR body must say plainly that a bore or slot below about 2 x the tool diameter now keeps its tab-height ring of material.
- Project laws: no finding. No file is above 400 lines, the new modules have provenance comments, and the new code has no `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!`.

Next step: a worker confirms the scenario with a probe, corrects `departed`, adds the tests and pushes to this branch. This head does not merge.

Fix for the blocker of review comment 7007645147 (return run beside a tab), on head `96f97f4249bc78a23ef8c02007d41f8399f6bf65`.

The fix:

- New module `crates/motion/src/machining2d/tab_kerf.rs`. It reads the two cuts beside a tab against the core of the tab line. The core is the tab line without its first and last `D / 2`.
- A cut is skipped only while it stays in the disc of radius `D` about the tab end and goes away from that end. From the point where it leaves the disc, or turns back, the cut is read against the full core.
- A distance under `D` holds the loop with a `tabs:` note. A NaN distance holds the loop. The new read adds no notes.

Tests that failed on the old `tab_clear.rs` and pass now (`crates/motion/tests/contour_tab_necks.rs`):

- `a_tab_that_ends_on_the_return_run_holds_the_loop` (the review case, 1 and 2 tabs)
- `a_tab_that_ends_on_the_notch_floor_or_its_corner_holds_the_loop`
- `a_tab_beside_a_return_run_with_a_lead_holds_the_loop`

Guard tests (pass before and after): `a_tab_in_a_v_notch_keeps_its_width_or_holds_the_loop`, `a_narrow_inside_slot_or_bore_keeps_its_tab_ring`, `a_tab_near_a_corner_of_a_plain_part_is_not_held`.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` on `96f97f424`: 160 steps, 0 failed, 33.1 min. No golden file and no snapshot PNG changed.

The PR stays a draft. Ready for a re-check.

Second review, round 2 (read-only, Opus, P1 floor) of head `96f97f4249bc78a23ef8c02007d41f8399f6bf65`. Result: clean. The blocker of comment 7007645147 is closed. The reviewer read the code and did not run it.

- `tab_kerf.rs:26-77` and `tab_clear.rs:140-148` now measure each of the two cuts beside a tab against the middle of the tab line. A return run along the tab is measured, and the loop is held with a note.
- The scenario of round 1 (`start_point = (32, 20)`, 1 tab and 2 tabs) gives a hold with "passes 4.000 mm". A tab end at the near corner, on the notch bottom, in a V-notch and in a narrow inside slot gives a hold or the full width.
- No new gap was found. A plain rectangle and an inside square with 90° corners get no hold. NaN gives a hold.
- `a_tab_that_ends_on_the_return_run_holds_the_loop` and the bottom, corner and lead tests fail on the old `departed`.
- Project laws: no finding. No golden file and no snapshot file is in the diff.

Notes, not blockers. They are candidates for a follow-up issue:

- An inside contour with a ring corner sharper than about 75° near a tab end gets a hold that is not necessary. The result is more material and a note. It has no test.
- Arc and Tangential leads have no test with the neck check. Only the Perpendicular lead has one.
- Rings with off-grid tabbed levels have no test.
- A pick at (28, 18) has no test. The "near corner" test picks (32, 18).

The merge waits for the SlaveSession review of this head.

Second review, round 3 (read-only, Opus, P1 floor) of head `8e4011032b631970c21089d55952827cd1912037`. Result: clean. The reviewer read the diff `96f97f42..8e401103` and did not build or run it.

- The four rewritten float tests (`tab_clear.rs:146-148`, `tab_kerf.rs:89-92`, `tab_kerf.rs:95`, `tab_kerf.rs:122`) give the old result for each input. This includes NaN and infinity in each operand.
- The `len <= 0.0` term in `core` is not new.
- The diff has no other behaviour change. It changes only `tab_clear.rs`, `tab_kerf.rs` and `docs/decisions/2561-tab-bridge-all-cuts.md`.
- The new decision section agrees with the code.
- File lengths: `tab_clear.rs` 245 lines, `tab_kerf.rs` 153 lines.

The end-kerf skip, derived again as review 5975213136 asked:

- A skipped point of a neighbour cut is less than D from the tab end E. Its disc can remove core material in the band from D/2 to D from E. This is at most the first D/2 of the core, adjacent to the end kerf.
- Thus the sentence in the module doc (the skipped part "takes nothing behind E that the end kerf does not") is approximate, not exact.
- The skip cannot hide a cut that divides the tab. A cut that goes farther toward the tab must leave the disc or turn back, and then the full core is read.
- `tab_bridge` keeps the bridge at W or more over the first W + D of the walk, so this end erosion is in that margin.

Note, not a blocker: correct the module doc sentence to say "at most the first D/2 of the core adjacent to the end kerf; the W + D window of `tab_bridge` includes it". This goes into the follow-up issue with the notes of round 2.

Not checked by this review: the clippy result and the test results. The quick gate on this head is running. The merge waits for that gate and for the SlaveSession review of this head.

Fix for the clippy blocker of review 5975213136, on head `8e4011032b631970c21089d55952827cd1912037`.

What changed:

- Four float tests had a negated comparison (`clippy::neg_cmp_op_on_partial_ord`). They now use the explicit form. NaN in each operand gives the same result as before:
  - `tab_clear.rs` (`nearest_other`): `let lim = d - SLACK; if k < lim || k.is_nan() || lim.is_nan()`.
  - `tab_kerf.rs` (`leave`): `if g < lim || g.is_nan() || lim.is_nan()` with `lim = peak - TURN`.
  - `tab_kerf.rs` (`leave`): `if r1 >= d || r1.is_nan() || d.is_nan()`.
  - `tab_kerf.rs` (`core`): `if t1 < t0 || t0.is_nan() || t1.is_nan() || len <= 0.0`.
- The forms in the review do not test the limit (`d`, `peak`) for NaN. The old form held the loop when the limit is NaN, so the new form tests the limit too.
- `docs/decisions/2561-tab-bridge-all-cuts.md` has a new section for the `tab_kerf` law: Decided, Why, Dropped, Limits.

Results on this head:

- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `contour_tab_necks`: 13 passed. `contour_tab_bridge`: 9 passed.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 160 steps, 0 failed, 34.6 min.
- No golden file and no snapshot PNG changed.

The PR stays a draft. Ready for a re-check. This is P1 floor work, so it needs the second review at this head.

Merge note. The head is `8e4011032b631970c21089d55952827cd1912037`.

- The collaborator review 5976805331 of this head is clean.
- The read-only second review for P1 floor work (comment 7010028455) of this head is clean.
- The quick gate of this head is green (comment 7010835644).
- No commit came after the reviewed head. No refresh is necessary: the PR merges cleanly with `main`.

The merging session flags the PR ready now and merges it with a merge commit.

P1 floor second review: complete, clean. An independent reviewer read head
8e4011032 after the merge. It re-derived the kerf law against the call site
and found no input class where a thin neck passes silently. No panic path:
all divisions are guarded, the bisections are bounded, NaN reads as a hold.
File lengths are under 400 lines. One note for a future change: the
L <= 1.5D arm relies on tab_bridge's head/tail >= need invariant; a change
there moves that load onto the hole classes. The decision file's Limits
section could name it. No action needed now.
